items.name: Add eval_mode to EvalConfig (type, TOML, merge, default)
items.description: Introduce the three-valued eval_mode config on each phase's eval block so behavior can be driven by mode instead of the enable_eval_output boolean. This is the foundation every other item reads.
steps: Add field `EvalMode string `json:"eval_mode"`` to EvalConfig in state/types.go (values: report|direct|conversational).
Add `EvalMode *string `toml:"eval_mode"`` to tomlEvalConfig in state/config.go (pointer so 'unset' is distinguishable).
In mergeEvalConfig, apply `if src.EvalMode != nil { dst.EvalMode = *src.EvalMode }`.
In DefaultForgeConfig, seed `EvalMode: "report"` on Specifying.Eval, Planning.Eval, and Implementing.Eval (mirror existing default-seeding pattern).
Leave EnableEvalOutput in place for back-compat; do not remove it (state-persistence schema is out of scope for this plan).

tests.description: DefaultForgeConfig seeds eval_mode="report" on specifying.eval, planning.eval, and implementing.eval.
A [<phase>.eval] TOML block with eval_mode="direct" overrides the default and is locked into the state file at init.
Omitting eval_mode in TOML leaves the default value (pointer-nil source does not zero the destination).

items.name: Validate eval_mode values in ValidateConfig
items.description: Reject configs whose eval_mode is not one of report|direct|conversational, mirroring the commit_strategy validation pattern, so bad config is caught at init.
steps: In ValidateConfig (state/config.go), define the valid set {report, direct, conversational}.
For each of specifying.eval, planning.eval, implementing.eval: if eval_mode != "" and not in the set, append `"<phase>.eval.eval_mode: invalid value %q"`.
Treat empty eval_mode as valid (the resolution helper supplies the back-compat default).

tests.description: ValidateConfig returns no violation for eval_mode values report, direct, and conversational.
ValidateConfig reports a violation for eval_mode="verbose" (or any value outside the set) naming the phase.
ValidateConfig accepts an empty eval_mode without violation.

items.name: EvalModeFor resolution helper with back-compat
items.description: Single source of truth for the effective eval mode, honoring legacy enable_eval_output so already-locked sessions keep their current behavior. Used by advance gating and all output rendering.
steps: Add `func EvalModeFor(ec EvalConfig, gen GeneralConfig) string` to the state package: return ec.EvalMode if non-empty; else "report" when ec.EnableEvalOutput || gen.EnableEvalOutput; else "conversational".
Add a ForgeState convenience method that selects the current phase's eval block (specifying/planning/implementing) and returns EvalModeFor for it.
Document that report is the default for new sessions and conversational preserves legacy enable_eval_output:false behavior.

tests.description: EvalModeFor returns the explicit eval_mode when set (report/direct/conversational).
With empty eval_mode and enable_eval_output=true, EvalModeFor returns "report".
With empty eval_mode and enable_eval_output=false (legacy locked session), EvalModeFor returns "conversational".

items.name: Gate --eval-report on eval_mode in advance transitions
items.description: Replace the enable_eval_output gating of --eval-report with eval_mode=="report" in EVALUATE, CROSS_REFERENCE_EVAL, and RECONCILE_EVAL, and emit the spec-worded ignore warning for non-report modes.
steps: In state/advance.go EVALUATE handling (~91-115), resolve mode via EvalModeFor. When report and EvalReport=="", error `--eval-report is required in EVALUATE state`. When mode != report and EvalReport != "", warn `--eval-report is ignored, --eval-report is only used in report mode`.
Apply the same change to CROSS_REFERENCE_EVAL (~187-211) and RECONCILE_EVAL (~245) handlers, with state-named required errors.
Keep `checkEvalReportExists` for report paths supplied in report mode; keep the always-required --verdict check unchanged.

tests.description: In report mode, advancing from EVALUATE with --verdict but no --eval-report errors with exit code 1.
In report mode, --eval-report pointing to a non-existent file errors naming the path.
In direct/conversational mode, --eval-report is accepted-but-ignored with warning `--eval-report is ignored, --eval-report is only used in report mode` and the advance proceeds.

items.name: Align cmd-layer advance warnings to spec wording
items.description: Make the cmd/advance.go pre-advance warnings consistent with the eval_mode gating and the exact spec wording, without double-printing the state-layer warning.
steps: In printAdvanceWarnings (cmd/advance.go), resolve the current phase eval_mode via EvalModeFor instead of branching on EnableEvalOutput; ensure the --eval-report warning is emitted in exactly one layer (state vs cmd) to avoid duplicate output.

Add CROSS_REFERENCE_EVAL to the warning's `evalStates` map (advance.go:234-237 currently lists only EVALUATE and RECONCILE_EVAL), so the `--eval-report is ignored ...` warning fires for cross-reference eval too.
Change the --message warning string to `--message is ignored, commits are not enabled` (keep the COMPLETE/ACCEPT/IMPLEMENT/COMMIT gate and !EnableCommits condition).
Confirm the warning text does not instruct how to enable commits (per spec invariants).

tests.description: advance --message with enable_commits=false at COMMIT prints `--message is ignored, commits are not enabled` and proceeds.
advance --eval-report in CROSS_REFERENCE_EVAL in a non-report mode prints the spec-worded ignore warning.
The --eval-report ignore warning is printed exactly once (not duplicated by both cmd and state layers).

items.name: Add specifying EVALUATE eval output (PrintSpecEvalOutput)
items.description: Fix the gap where `forgectl eval` in specifying EVALUATE falls through to the default error: add the routing case and a PrintSpecEvalOutput that embeds evaluators.SpecEval (currently embedded-but-unused).
steps: Add `func PrintSpecEvalOutput(w io.Writer, s *ForgeState, projectRoot string) error` to state/output.go: print `=== SPEC EVALUATION ROUND n/m ===`, Domain/Batch header, `--- EVALUATOR INSTRUCTIONS ---` with evaluators.SpecEval, and `--- SPECS TO EVALUATE ---` listing the batch spec filenames, topics, and full file paths.
Add the routing case to cmd/eval.go before the planning/implementing case: `case s.Phase == state.PhaseSpecifying && s.State == state.StateEvaluate: return state.PrintSpecEvalOutput(...)`.
Defer the per-mode REPORT OUTPUT / PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS sections to evalmode.eval-output-modes (this item establishes the function and routing).

tests.description: `forgectl eval` in specifying EVALUATE prints `=== SPEC EVALUATION ROUND` with evaluators.SpecEval contents and the batch spec list.
`forgectl eval` outside an eval state still errors naming the current state (no regression to the default branch).

items.name: Per-mode action and status text for all eval-entry states
items.description: Render the advance/status Action line according to eval_mode for every state that enters an evaluation: EVALUATE (specifying/planning/implementing), CROSS_REFERENCE_EVAL, and RECONCILE_EVAL — matching the report/direct/conversational variants in the specs.
steps: In state/output.go EVALUATE rendering (specifying ~98-117, planning ~490-503, implementing ~840-870), branch on the resolved eval_mode.
report: action ends with `advance with --verdict PASS|FAIL --eval-report <path>`.

direct: action says spawn a sub-agent to `evaluate and correct`, note `<spec|batch|plan> files have been staged. Sub-agent makes corrections directly.`, and ends with `advance with --verdict PASS|FAIL`.
conversational: action ends with `advance with --verdict PASS|FAIL` (no report path, no staged-files note).

Apply the SAME three-mode branch to the action text for ENTERING CROSS_REFERENCE_EVAL (spec-lifecycle.md 299-340) and ENTERING RECONCILE_EVAL (spec-reconciliation.md 65-97): report keeps `--eval-report <path>`; direct uses the `evaluate and correct ... files have been staged` wording and drops `--eval-report`; conversational drops the report path. These two states render single-form today (output.go ~193-209 and the reconcile-eval renderer) and must be migrated too.
Apply the per-mode branch to the compact `status` output for all of these states.

tests.description: Planning EVALUATE in report mode renders an action ending with `--eval-report <path>`; in conversational mode it ends with `--verdict PASS|FAIL` and no report path.
Implementing EVALUATE in direct mode renders `evaluate and correct` plus the staged-files note.

Entering CROSS_REFERENCE_EVAL and RECONCILE_EVAL renders the matching per-mode action text (report includes `--eval-report <path>`; direct includes the staged-files/`evaluate and correct` note; conversational has neither).
status output for an eval-entry state matches the same per-mode variant as advance.

items.name: Per-mode REFINE and IMPLEMENT re-entry action text
items.description: Extend the existing 2-way (report/conversational) REFINE branching to 3-way on eval_mode, add the direct arm, and cover specifying REFINE and the implementing IMPLEMENT after-eval re-entry text.
steps: In state/output.go REFINE rendering (planning ~516, implementing ~822), switch from EnableEvalOutput to the resolved eval_mode with three arms: report -> `Study the eval file %q and implement any corrections as needed.`; direct -> `Review unstaged changes from the evaluator (git diff). Accept, revise, or revert corrections as needed.`; conversational -> `Make corrections based off communication with the evaluator.`
Add the same 3-way branch to specifying REFINE rendering.
Apply the same three arms to the implementing IMPLEMENT after-eval re-entry action text (batch-implementation.md rounds 2+).
Preserve the shared `Apply "fresh" eyes and a tightened lens ...` line on all arms where the specs include it.

tests.description: Planning REFINE in direct mode renders `Review unstaged changes from the evaluator (git diff).`
Specifying REFINE in conversational mode renders `Make corrections based off communication with the evaluator.`
Implementing IMPLEMENT after-eval re-entry in report mode renders `Study the eval file`.

items.name: Per-mode REPORT OUTPUT and PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS in all eval-context output
items.description: Make every eval-context output function render the REPORT OUTPUT and PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS sections according to eval_mode, and backfill the previous-evaluations section where it is currently missing.
steps: Across PrintEvalOutput (planning + implementing), PrintReconcileEvalOutput, PrintCrossRefEvalOutput, and PrintSpecEvalOutput, branch the trailing sections on the resolved eval_mode.
report: `--- REPORT OUTPUT ---` with `Write your evaluation report to:\n  <path>`; `--- PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS ---` listing prior rounds with verdict and report path.
direct: `--- REPORT OUTPUT ---` with `Make corrections directly to the <spec|batch|plan> files.`; `--- PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS ---` listing prior rounds with verdict and `(direct corrections)`.
conversational: omit both `--- REPORT OUTPUT ---` and `--- PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS ---`.
Add the PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS section to PrintReconcileEvalOutput and PrintCrossRefEvalOutput where it is currently absent.

tests.description: Planning eval output in report mode includes `--- REPORT OUTPUT ---` with `Write your evaluation report to:` and a PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS section on round 2+.
Eval output in direct mode includes `Make corrections directly to the plan files.` (and the batch/spec variants for implementing/specifying).
Eval output in conversational mode omits both REPORT OUTPUT and PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS sections.
Reconcile and cross-reference eval output in report mode include a PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS section on round 2+.
Reconcile and cross-reference eval output in direct mode render prior rounds as `(direct corrections)` in PREVIOUS EVALUATIONS on round 2+.
